hale.heading: hale: A fine day's work, Captain. Nell reckons we raise the wreck-waters by morning.
hale: If there's nothing else, you might turn in. The crew will want you fresh. And shouting.
hale.s1: hale: Morning, Captain. Rough swell in the night, but she rode it well. Nell has us back on course.
hale: Squawks went out on his morning flight at dawn. He'll be back when he's hungry, or when he's thought of something rude to say.
hale[concerned]: And Barnacle Bob is off punishment duty. I apologise in advance.
hale.s2: hale: I've put the new man on the foredeck with Sully. Swabbing.
hale[resigned]: He asked what the pay structure was for swabbing. I told him the structure was 'no'.
hale.s3: hale[concerned]: Captain, did you hear that noise at lunch? Half the ship did. Mags thought the stove had gone up.
hale: ...That doesn't make me feel better, sir.

then: hale[coughing]: Rook has the line, Captain. We haul the moment you tug. Or the moment you stop moving.
hale: Bring him back, sir. The ship's not the ship without him shouting at it.
else: hale[coughing]: Everyone's up and accounted for, Captain. Except my sense of smell. That's gone overboard.

hale.s5: hale: Squawks is resting with the Doc. He's... very pink, Captain.
hale[resigned]: The men want to know when we can open the hatches again. I said we'd open them when they stop opening themselves.
hale.s6: hale[annoyed]: The treasure, sir. The men are saying all of it. Is it all of it?
hale: Then I'll keep the men away from Guzzlegut. For his sake, not theirs.
hale.tr: hale: I'll keep the jury from hanging the defendant until we've seen off the navy, Captain. After that I make no promises.
hale.s8: hale: The rowboat protocol's posted on the mainmast, Captain. One rumble, one rowboat, half a mile.
hale[smug]: The men learned it faster than their knots. I've added 'Listening for Garrick' to the watch bill. It's the most popular post aboard.
quill.s1: quill: Morning, Captain. Ledger's balanced, stores are counted, and the prisoner has asked for a lawyer again.
captain: Tell him we have an excellent lawyer. It's a plank.
quill: I'll phrase it more gently, sir.
quill.s2: quill[concerned]: Captain, the new man asked to see the ledger. He called it 'the books'. He said it with such... affection.
quill: I've locked it in the strongbox. And locked the strongbox in the treasure room. And kept the key in my shoe.
quill.s3: quill[disgusted]: He ate the stores, Captain. Not some of the stores. The idea of stores.
quill: I've entered it as 'Lunch (Guzzlegut)'. It takes up a page.
quill.s4: quill[coughing]: I have my ledger over my face, Captain. It's the only thing aboard that still smells of ink.
quill: I'm recording this as weather.
quill.s5: quill: Squawks will live, the Doc says. I've started a new column: 'Feathers, lost'. The number is upsetting.
quill.s6: quill[devastated]: Four thousand two hundred and eleven coins, Captain. Twelve years of plunder. And I can't in good conscience write down what they're worth.
quill.tr: quill: I'm clerk of the court, Captain. I've written the charges out neatly. It helps.
quill.s8: quill: I've opened an account for Mister Guzzlegut. It's in the red. It will always be in the red. I find that soothing.
quill: And the treasure's still counted, sir. Still aboard. Still worthless. I count it anyway. Habit.
mags.s1: mags: Morning, Captain! Salty Jim's back on the galley, so I've someone to argue with who isn't Quill.
mags[laugh]: He's pickled everything that stood still. I caught him eyeing Wick.
mags.s2: mags[annoyed]: That fellow from the bathtub came in asking what the menu was. It's stew, I told him.
mags: He asked if there was a tasting menu. There is. It's stew.
mags.s3: mags[disgusted]: Twenty years I've cooked for pirates, Captain. I've never watched a man eat like that.
mags: And then his belly spoke. My pans are still ringing.
mags.s4: mags[coughing]: My galley! My clean galley! It smells like a cheese died in a boot!
mags[angry]: When this clears, that man is on bread and water. No. Just water. Bread's too risky.
mags.s5: mags[concerned]: Poor Squawks. Not a feather on him, and shivering.
mags: I've some red wool put by. I'm going to knit him something. Don't tell him. He'll bite me.
mags.s6: mags[angry]: The treasure too? Of course the treasure too.
mags: I'd have fed that man to the fish, Captain, but the fish have suffered enough.
mags.tr: mags[happy]: The sweater's done! Little holes for his wings and a bobble on the hat.
mags[laugh]: He hates it. He's wearing it anyway. That's how you know it's warm.
mags.s8: mags: New rule in my galley: Garrick eats on deck, downwind, facing the sea.
mags[laugh]: He says it's discrimination. I say it's ventilation.
fennimore.s1: fennimore: Morning, Captain. Ned's back on his feet after the ague. Foot, rather.
fennimore: I recommended rest. He recommended I mind my own business. A healthy sign.
fennimore.s2: fennimore: I examined our castaway. Sound heart, sound lungs, a terrifying appetite, and a firm belief that the sea owes him money.
fennimore.s3: fennimore[concerned]: I heard his stomach from the sick bay, Captain. Through two decks.
fennimore: Medically speaking, that isn't a stomach. That's a weather system.
fennimore.s4: fennimore[coughing]: Nothing in my cabinet for this, Captain. I checked twice.
fennimore: I have a salve for everything except whatever this is.
fennimore.s5: fennimore: The bird will live. He lost ninety feathers in a hundred. They'll grow back in a month or so. Keep him warm until then.
fennimore[smug]: I've prescribed rest, broth, and not looking in mirrors.
fennimore.s6: fennimore: I've inspected the crew. Lungs, fine. Morale, not. I have no tincture for gold that smells.
fennimore.tr: fennimore: I'm here in a medical capacity, Captain. In case the jury gets excited. Or the defendant does.
fennimore.s8: fennimore: I'm keeping a log of Mister Guzzlegut's... events. Purely scientific.
fennimore[smug]: There's a paper in it. Possibly a warning to the whole of medicine.
brask.s1: brask: MORNING, CAPTAIN! Guns clean, sea calm, nobody to shoot! TERRIBLE!
brask.s2: brask: THAT NEW FELLOW ASKED ME WHAT A CANNON COSTS! I told him! He asked if I'd take LESS!
brask.s3: brask[surprised]: WAS THAT A GUN? Sounded like a twelve-pounder! Below decks!
brask.s4: brask[coughing]: I CAN'T HEAR A THING, CAPTAIN, BUT I CAN SMELL IT!
brask[laugh]: First time my ears got the better deal!
brask.s5: brask: THE BIRD'S BALD! Looks like a boiled chicken! Don't tell him I said that!
brask[alarmed]: HE HEARD ME. HE'S GLARING.
brask.s6: brask[annoyed]: RUINED THE TREASURE? I'll load HIM into Margaret! She's never fired a man before! She'd enjoy it!
brask.tr: brask: GUNS READY, CAPTAIN! Just say the word! Is the word 'FIRE'? I LIKE that word!
brask.s8: brask: They're calling it the Yellow Broadside down in the gunroom! Best shot this ship ever fired and it wasn't even a GUN!
brask[laugh]: When his belly rumbles I ring the bell! TWO bells for ROWBOAT!
nell.heading: nell: We'll raise the wreck-waters by morning, Captain. The old charts say a galleon went down there with a full hold.
nell[smug]: The charts are forty years out of date. So is the galleon.
nell.s1: nell: Bang on course, Captain. The swell pushed us a mile east in the night. I pushed us back.
nell.s2: nell[smug]: A man in a bathtub, two leagues from any land. I checked the charts. There's no bathtub marked anywhere.
nell.s3: nell: Clear skies all round, Captain. So whatever that thunder was, it didn't come from the sky.
nell.s4: nell[coughing]: I'm staying at the helm, Captain. The wind's carrying it forward, so back here I'm the only one breathing.
nell: I'd like that noted when the shares are counted.
nell.s5: nell: We're making way, slower than I'd like. The fumes got into the sails. They belly out wrong.
nell.s6: nell[annoyed]: Twelve years of prize money gone yellow. I was going to buy a house with a garden.
nell: Now I'll settle for a house with a window I can open.
nell.tr: nell: The helm's ready when you are, Captain. She's yours whenever you want her.
nell.s8: nell: New standing order: we sail with the wind on the beam. That way the smell goes sideways.
wick.s1: wick[happy]: Morning, Captain! Barnacle Bob says lamp oil tastes like spicy sunshine! Is that true?
wick.s2: wick[happy]: Captain, the bathtub man says he's a businessman! He gave me his card!
wick: It says 'Garrick'. On a biscuit.
wick.s3: wick[surprised]: Captain, his stomach made a noise like a whale! I've never heard a whale. But it was like one!
wick.s4: wick[coughing]: My eyes are watering and I'm not even sad! Is this what the navy smells like?
wick.s5: wick[sad]: Squawks won't talk to anyone, Captain. I said he looked nice pink.
wick.s6: wick[concerned]: Is it true the gold's ruined? Even the crown? I was going to try it on one day. Just for a minute.
wick.tr: wick[happy]: I'm on the jury, Captain! I've never been on a jury! Do I get a hat?
wick.s8: wick[laugh]: I'm listening for Mister Guzzlegut's stomach on the morning watch! If I hear it, I shout ROWBOAT!
rook.s1: rook: Morning, Cap'n. Capstan's greased. Bob tried to drink the grease. Separately from the lamp oil.
rook.s2: rook[laugh]: The new man offered to 'consult' on the hauling. Stood at the back and said 'heave' like a banker.
rook.s3: rook[concerned]: That noise, Cap'n. I heard one like it once, off a volcano.
rook: A small volcano. Smaller than him.
rook.s4: rook[coughing]: I've carried barrels, cannons and Barnacle Bob up that ladder, Cap'n. Never carried a smell before. It follows you up.
rook.s5: rook: Line held, Cap'n. You came out heavier than you went in. That'll be the bird. And the smell.
rook.s6: rook[annoyed]: Say the word, Cap'n, and he walks the plank. I'll make him a new one. A short one.
rook.tr: rook: On the jury, Cap'n. I've already decided. Just waiting for you to finish talking.
rook.s8: rook[laugh]: Lowering the rowboat's my job now. Eleven seconds from 'ROWBOAT' to splash.
rook: The navy can't launch a boat in eleven seconds. I asked one.
sully.s1: sully: Morning, Captain. Swabbing. Again. There's a lesson in it somewhere.
sully.s2: sully[annoyed]: Hale gave me a helper, Captain. He's been supervising my plank for an hour.
sully: The plank's doing fine. I'm not.
sully.s3: sully: I'm not a man who's easily impressed, Captain. But that lunch. That lunch was an achievement.
sully.s4: sully[coughing]: I'm swabbing the air, Captain. It's not working. Still the most useful thing I've done all week.
sully.s5: sully[sad]: Found a red feather by the hatch, Captain. I'm keeping it for him. In case he wants it back.
sully.s6: sully[annoyed]: No treasure, no shares. So I've been swabbing for free all these years? Someone might have said. I'd have stopped.
sully.tr: sully: Jury duty. It's like swabbing, except you sit down and get to be angry.
sully.s8: sully: The rowboat protocol's the best rule we've got. Every time his stomach growls, we all stop work.
sully[happy]: I've never been so rested.
finch.s1: finch: The sea's holding her breath again, Captain. Something's coming. Something... floating.
finch.s2: finch[concerned]: A man in a bathtub, Captain. The sea didn't drown him. She spat him out.
finch.s3: finch: Did you hear it, Captain? Deep, like something waking up under the hull.
finch[concerned]: The sea's worried. I've never known her worried.
finch.s4: finch[coughing]: Forty years at sea, Captain. I've been cursed by the sea plenty. Never by a person.
finch.s5: finch: The bird went in feathered and came out naked. That's a sign, Captain.
finch: I don't know of what. But it's a sign.
finch.s6: finch: Cursed treasure, Captain. I always said it would be.
finch: I never said it would be cursed like this.
finch.tr: finch: I've seen the navy run from storms, from reefs, from you, Captain. Never from a sail.
finch.s8: finch[happy]: The sea's let out her breath at last, Captain. And so, frequently, has Mister Guzzlegut.
finch: Gulls won't come near us now. Fish neither. First peaceful watch I've had in forty years.
jory.s1: jory: Morning, Captain. The swell sprang two of my patches below. Sorted. The hull's grumbling, but she always grumbles.
jory.s2: jory: Our castaway asked me to appraise his bathtub.
jory: I appraised it. It's a bathtub.
jory.s3: jory[alarmed]: The hull flexed at lunch, Captain. I felt it through my boots.
jory: Hulls don't flex at lunch.
jory.s4: jory[coughing]: The blast sprung the treasure door clean off its pins, Captain. I'll mend it. When I can breathe near it.
jory.s5: jory: I'll rehang the treasure door once the air's thinner. Planks, nails and a great deal of vinegar.
jory.s6: jory: Door's patched, Captain. I scrubbed the planks three times. They're clean.
jory: They're also still yellow. Wood remembers.
jory.tr: jory: Built the defendant a little platform to stand on, Captain. Very sturdy. I checked twice. He's heavier than he looks.
jory.s8: jory: Built him a rowboat rack. Quick release: pull the pin, down she goes.
jory: I'm proud of it. I'm ashamed of being proud of it.
